demonstrated_checks: Unknown sheet names and opaque malformed worksheet/shared-string canaries did not appear in receipts or change approved envelope semantics; only declared whole-object observed bytes/digests were excluded from semantic comparison.
Instrumented ZIP reads opened exactly the four approved envelope members; no worksheet/shared-string content was opened or decompressed.
Unsafe paths, duplicate ZIP entries, duplicate sheet/relationship identifiers and external/traversal workbook targets produced constant blocked outcomes without source text.
UTF-8 and UTF-16 DTD/entity fixtures, over-limit member count, actual decompressed byte count and XML depth were rejected.
Descriptor-relative read/write helpers rejected symlinks, conflicting outputs and oversized reads without changing existing fixture files; new fixture files used mode0600.
Ignored source-path rejection preceded git and transport calls; global socket creation and DNS were forbidden throughout all tests.
Redirect near-matches, userinfo, fragments, changed paths/hosts/schemes and second redirects were rejected; fake redirect bodies were not read or followed.
Mutating nested inventory data in a public synthetic receipt no longer changed trusted module inventory.

Closed capture-receipt validation rejected extra keys, altered actions/modes/commit shape, bool-as-int and float-as-int substitutions, false exposure claims, invented counts and duplicate JSON keys before the fake object-read boundary.
limitations: No production GET, real workbook, existing scientific cache, registration, allocation or numerical outcome was accessed.
Filesystem tests used only new temporary fixture directories under this ignored review directory.
Capture-receipt tests used a fake source context and fake cache reader, deliberately stopping before any object read.
This review does not establish actual source availability, OOXML compatibility, data pairing, independence, scientific readiness or successful production execution.
Author-owned test results, future CI, reviewed-commit guards in a committed production checkout and real capture/envelope replay remain separate evidence.
promotion_note: Independent test loader supports either ignored candidate or tracked scripts; the production guard test explicitly patches __file__ to an ignored path and forbids git/transport, so promotion does not activate production capture.
root_identified_issues_rechecked: Nested EXPECTED_INVENTORY alias fixed by detached copies; independently tested.
Capture-receipt subset validation replaced with closed canonical/type/flag/null checks; independently tested.
scope: Ignored candidate source and independent synthetic fixtures only; not an authorization receipt for production capture or a claim that capture occurred.

source_review.bounded_execution: Raw source cap, ZIP member count, actual decompression caps, XML depth/nodes/attributes and closed namespace/profile checks are explicit. Unsupported layouts remain blocked.
source_review.projection: Recognized roles are restricted to References and Column Descriptions presence/ordinal. Source strings remain inside the machine custodian; no raw worksheet/dictionary or source-token output route exists.
source_review.scientific_status: Envelope status remains BLOCKED_SCHEMA with null row/paired/group/overlap counts, no fits/splits and no sampling-independence claim.
source_review.source_and_capture_identity: Fixed inventory metadata is checked by canonical-byte identity. Whole-buffer size/MD5 is checked before capture success; captured SHA-256 is rechecked before envelope parsing. These checks do not establish physical validity.
source_review.workflow_guard_scope: The guards constrain normal workflow and do not claim to defend against hostile Python code or a malicious process owner.
